incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: embeddings-us-east p99 latency > 2s (alert-id: emb-us-e-2026-03-15-01). Primary: Devon (on-call). Please ack and triage.

Devon (on-call): acked. I'm on it but need to handoff at 07:15 UTC — leaving early. Quick summary: we saw a spike in p99 for embeddings region after a bursty client. KV cache miss rate up ~35%, batcher queues grew. No full outage, but elevated tail latency and some 429s. I'll leave a short playbook for Priya.

Priya (secondary): thanks. I'll take primary at 07:15. Can you list immediate checks and anything I should run first?

Devon (on-call): sure — quick checklist before I go: 
- Confirm KV pods are healthy and not OOM/killed. 
- Restart batcher pods if queue depth > 500. 
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size to lower latency if restart doesn't help.
- Enable per-key rate limiting for the affected client (if they surface).

Devon (on-call): run these cmds for diagnostics:
```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=kvcache -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=kvcache -c cache --tail=200
kubectl -n inference top pods | grep kvcache
kubectl -n inference get hpa -l app=batcher -o yaml
```

Devon (on-call): if you need a quick restart:
```bash
kubectl -n inference delete pod -l app=batcher --grace-period=0 --force
# then watch queue drain
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=batcher -c batcher --follow
```

Priya (secondary): got it. Any runbook links? Also, do we have a lite hotpatch if the restart doesn't clear tail?

Devon (on-call): runbooks: 
- Embedding tail latency: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embedding-tail-latency
- KV cache anomalies: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-miss-and-warmup
- Batcher thrashing: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batcher-thrash-playbook

Devon (on-call): hotpatch options (short): 
1) Reduce max_batch_size for embeddings route to 4: edit ConfigMap 
2) Apply temporary model-quantization fallback (model-v1.3-lite) for the heavy client via routing policy: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood/api/v1/routes/route-embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"override_model":"model-v1.3-lite","priority":10}'
```
3) Enable prefix caching for known repeated inputs per runbook.

Jules (oncall-support): adding link to quick commands doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/oncall-quick-commands (contains kubectl snippets + hpa tweaks). Also tagging Sam and Marta for visibility.

Sam (SRE): quick check: look at infra-side metrics for network stalls — rare but worth ruling out. `ss -s` on cache nodes and `dmesg` for OOM/kills. If you see socket drops, escalate to eng-infra.

Marta (SRE): I'll keep an eye on autoscaler and infra health for 30m. If the HPA flaps, that can cause transient latency.

Priya (secondary): taking primary now. Checklist I'm following: 
- run kvcache logs, check restart count 
- restart batcher pods if queue > 500 
- set temporary max_batch_size=4 for embeddings route (will test in canary) 
- throttle the offending client via rate-limit rule (if we identify them)

Priya (secondary): quick status after checks: KV cache pods show 2/3 restarts in last 10m, memory pressure on node pool-emb-2. Batcher queue currently ~780. I'm going to restart batcher pods 1-at-a-time.

Devon (on-call): +1 to 1-at-a-time. If restart doesn't reduce queue in 90s, apply batcher config rollback to previous revision. Steps to rollback: 
```bash
# get current image
kubectl -n inference get deployment batcher -o=jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
# rollback to previous image via patch or use k8s rollout revert if configured
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/batcher --to-revision=2
```

Priya (secondary): restarted batcher pods rolling. Queue down to 420 within 2 minutes — p99 trending down to 1.6s. Still warmup of KV cache.

Devon (on-call): good. For triage notes: customer impact limited to a small % getting 429s for embeddings-us-east between 06:42–07:05 UTC. Please create follow-up ticket with client ids and attach logs (kvcache logs + batcher tail).

Jules (oncall-support): creating ticket INF-2026-642 and assigning to recovery:eng. Priya, add any client ids you find. I'll add runbook pointers in the ticket.

Priya (secondary): noted. One more pointer for future: if KV warmup is the recurring issue, we should add a small pre-warm job that seeds cache after deploys/scale-ups. Adding to ticket as improvement.

Devon (on-call): leaving a small checklist in the ticket for the person taking the followup: 
- attach logs: `kvcache` tail 200, `batcher` traces, `metrics/p99` Grafana link 
- verify node memory pressure causes and consider scaling node pool or OOM tuning 
- consider temporary routing to model-v1.3-lite for heavy clients until long-term fix

Priya (primary): acknowledged. I'm sticky on page for next 45m, will hand back at 08:00 UTC to Jules unless there's flare. Thanks Devon — enjoy the morning. :coffee:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager acknowledged and resolved — alert auto-closed after 20m of p99 recovery. Incident summary pinned to ticket INF-2026-642.

Devon (on-call): thanks team — leaving now. If anything pops, @Priya will be primary. Quick note in case of recurrence: hit runbook kvcache-miss-and-warmup first.

Priya (primary): copy. Follow-up ticket created and assigned. Closing thread after handoff. :lock_with_ink_pen:
